The growing number of connected devices in smart home environments has amplified security 
risks, particularly from Man-in-the-Middle (MitM) attacks. These attacks allow cybercriminals to 
intercept and manipulate communication streams between devices, often remaining undetected. 
Traditional rule-based methods struggle to cope with the complexity of these attacks, creating 
a need for more advanced, adaptive intrusion detection systems. This research introduces the 
AEXB Model, a hybrid deep learning approach that combines the feature extraction capabilities 
of an AutoEncoder with the classification power of XGBoost. By combining these complementary 
methods, the model enhances detection accuracy and significantly reduces false positives. The AEXB 
Model’s methodology encompasses robust preprocessing steps, including data cleaning, scaling, and 
dimensionality reduction, followed by comprehensive feature engineering and selection techniques, 
such as Recursive Feature Elimination (RFE) and correlation analysis. By applying this approach to the 
Intrusion Detection in Smart Home (IDSH) dataset, the model achieves an impressive 97.24% accuracy, 
demonstrating its effectiveness in identifying anomalous network behavior indicative of MitM attacks. 
Additionally, the model’s real-time detection capabilities allow for rapid responses to threats, thus 
providing continuous protection in dynamic smart home environments.

In cybersecurity, a Man-in-the-Middle (MitM) attack occurs when an attacker intercepts communication 
between two parties who believe they are directly communicating with each other. This type of attack is 
particularly dangerous, as it allows the attacker to eavesdrop and potentially capture sensitive information, such 
as login credentials and credit card numbers, or inject malicious content into the communication stream1,2. 
A MitM attack is commonly performed when the attacker secretly relays and alters the messages exchanged 
between a server and client such as login details. In the case of an online transaction, the attacker intercepts 
to network traffic between a user and the website capturing sensitive data or executing financial manipulation. 
These over-links of communication, such as Wi-Fi networks, email, or even within the SSL/TLS tunnel between 
a web browser and server-side can be compromised by an attacker enabling MitM3,4.
In all environments where trust, as well as confidentiality, are of the utmost concern MitM attacks play a role, 
which we cannot neglect at any time. Protective measures generally include the employ of encryption protocols, 
good strong authentication mechanisms used in conjunction with robust identity and access management 
services or tools; and real-time monitoring of network traffic flow for detecting anomalous activities. Even, 
MitM attacks still plague the cybersecurity landscape—bringing with them unpredictable challenges demanding 
additional security procedures to be followed strictly5,6. People and organizations need to realize what MitM 
attacks are for them to be able to protect their data, as well as the integrity of communications. By identifying the 
risks and taking all necessary precautions, businesses can protect the customer data that is entrusted to them, 
limit financial losses and keep their reputation. On a personal level, knowing the threat of MitM attacks prevents 
an individual from being manipulated to provide sensitive data like bank account information and private 
conversations may lessen the chances for identity theft and other forms of cybercrime7,8. The main feature of

Deep Learning as a cutting-edge technology has reshaped cybersecurity, including MitM attack detection 
and prevention. For such detection, DL can be far more useful, mainly because of the way DL works to find 
unusual complex patterns within network traffic. Sophisticated MitM attacks are hard to catch as they evolve 
advanced strategies and traditional rule-based systems cannot always recognize them18–20. Where DL models 
shine, however, by analyzing data across layers of the network and detecting subtle variations from normal 
behavior. It has improved detection accuracy to minimize false positives and the ratio of nuisance alerts, or false 
negatives in which real threats are sight unseen. Real-time detection of threats—Real-time tracking is one key 
benefit DL offers to prevent MitM attacks. Rather than spending time on performing manual analysis of data, 
DL algorithms can process and analyze live data then quickly. This real-time detection is vital to mitigate a MitM 
attack efficiently, providing security systems with the ability to trigger a prompt response by either containment 
or notification of administrators.

Main contributions of the work
This paper introduces the AEXB Model, a novel hybrid approach that addresses the identified challenges by 
integrating AutoEncoder and XGBoost algorithms. The main contributions of this work are as follows:
•	 We propose a unique combination of AutoEncoder for unsupervised feature extraction and dimensionality 
reduction with XGBoost for efficient classification. This hybrid model capitalizes on the strengths of both 
algorithms to enhance the detection and prevention of MitM attacks in real-time.
•	 The study implements comprehensive feature engineering techniques, including correlation analysis, tree-
based feature importance, and Recursive Feature Elimination (RFE). These methods are crucial for refining 
the dataset to include only the most significant features, thereby improving model accuracy and reducing 
computational overhead.
•	 By emphasizing real-time threat detection, the model ensures prompt identification and response to potential 
MitM attacks, which is essential for maintaining the security of communications within smart homes.
•	 Comprehensive Data Preprocessing: We utilize robust data preprocessing steps, including handling missing 
values with median imputation, scaling numerical features, and encoding categorical data. This thorough 
preprocessing is vital for optimizing the dataset for effective model training.
•	 The proposed model is designed to be scalable and adaptable, making it applicable to various IoT environ­
ments beyond smart homes, such as industrial control systems and healthcare networks, where cybersecurity 
is equally critical.
Although some of the related works have proposed utilizing machine learning or deep learning approaches to 
detect MitM attacks, this work is unique in the sense of incorporating the concepts of the unsupervised feature 
extraction and the supervised classification all in one framework and for the real-time detection of the intrusions 
within the smart home networks. Furthermore, the AEXB Model considers the scalability and adaptability issue 
and includes the flexibility of both data preprocessing and feature selection aspects in SID, which are not, covered 
in existing intrusion detection systems.

Methodology
The proposed methodology centres on the development of the AEXB Model, a hybrid approach that combines 
AutoEncoder for feature extraction and dimensionality reduction with XGBoost for classification. The 
methodology begins with the preprocessing of the Intrusion Detection in Smart Home (IDSH) dataset, involving 
steps such as handling missing values, scaling numerical features, and encoding categorical data. Advanced 
feature engineering and selection techniques, including correlation analysis, tree-based feature importance, and 
RFE, are applied to optimize the dataset’s quality. Figure 2 shows the architecture of the proposed model.

Handling missing values
In this study, missing values that have been treated have been handled by imputing feature medians to the 
respective features, a technique renowned for its effectiveness and ease of computation. APP: Median imputation

Detection in Smart Home (IDSH) dataset. Another method that may be used to fill in missing observations is the 
VMFCVD framework, where MV stands for Mean/Mode Function with Variable Deletion. VMFCVD makes its 
imputations based on the correlated variables, and since most value imputation methods focus on maintaining

design, as speed is essential in assessing the threat in real-time cybersecurity environments. Second, median

Conclusion and future work
This study presents the AEXB Model, a hybrid approach that integrates AutoEncoder and XGBoost to address the 
growing threat of Man-in-the-Middle (MitM) attacks in smart home environments. By leveraging AutoEncoder’s 
feature extraction and dimensionality reduction capabilities alongside XGBoost’s efficient classification, the 
model achieves superior accuracy and reliability in real-time intrusion detection, as evidenced by its 97.24% 
accuracy on the Intrusion Detection in Smart Home (IDSH) dataset. Comprehensive data preprocessing, 
feature engineering, and optimization techniques ensure robust performance, reducing both false positives and 
computational overhead. The AEXB Model’s scalability also makes it applicable to various IoT networks beyond 
smart homes, such as healthcare and industrial systems, where MitM attacks pose significant risks. Future work 
will explore the integration of additional deep learning models, such as convolutional neural networks (CNNs), 
to enhance feature extraction capabilities on larger datasets. Expanding the dataset to include a wider range 
of IoT devices and attack vectors will further validate the model’s scalability. Implementing the AEXB Model 
in real-time systems with continuous learning capabilities represents another promising avenue for mitigating 
evolving cyber threats, providing a comprehensive and adaptable solution to modern cybersecurity challenges.
